title: NaOH‐ and KOH‐activated cardboard waste carbons for methylene blue, malachite green, and rhodamine 6G removal: Isotherm, kinetics, and thermodynamics
content:
Abstract

This work aimed to evaluate the adsorptive properties of cardboard waste-based activated carbons for the removal of cationic dyes. The activated carbons were produced through activation using potassium hydroxide and sodium hydroxide, and were characterized for surface functional groups, specific surface area, and surface morphology. The relationship between the molecular structure of dyes and the properties of activated carbon was established to provide insight into removal selectivity. Batch adsorption was performed at varying concentrations, contact times, and solution temperatures. Results show that the mesoporous activated carbon produced by KOH activation, with a large specific surface area of 563 m2/g, exhibits high adsorption capacities of 98.2 mg/g (0.319 mmol/g), 311 mg/g (0.885 mmol/g), and 14.1 mg/g (0.0324 mmol/g) for methylene blue, malachite green, and rhodamine 6G, respectively. The equilibrium data could be described by the Langmuir model, while the kinetics fitted well into pseudo-first order and pseudo-second order models, suggesting monolayer coverage of molecules onto the carbon surface through physicochemical interactions. The adsorption of all cationic dyes onto the activated carbons is endothermic, favorable, and spontaneous at elevated solution temperatures.
